title: AI scams in Georgia and South Florida: How scammers use deepfakes to steal millions

reading.body:
Criminals are using deepfakes and voice cloning created with generative AI to impersonate trusted figures, including a South Florida immigration attorney whose identity was stolen to solicit payment from immigrants seeking legal services. The scams operate on social media and through phone calls, exploiting the difficulty of distinguishing AI-generated voices and images from authentic ones. No human verification step protected victims from sending money to fraudsters posing as licensed professionals or family members in emergencies.

This is impersonation enabled by AI synthesis tools deployed outside any protective system. The technology made fraud harder to detect because the cloned voices and fabricated images are sufficiently realistic to deceive people who know the person being impersonated. It is not established whether the deepfake generation tools were purpose-built for fraud or whether legitimate voice or image synthesis services were misused by the scammers.

summary:
# Summary

Criminals are increasingly using artificial intelligence technology to commit sophisticated scams across Georgia and South Florida. According to the FBI's 2025 Internet Crime Report, Americans lost nearly 893 million dollars to AI-enabled scams last year. Notable cases include a South Florida immigration attorney whose voice was cloned to target immigrants, and a Cobb County couple who lost approximately 800,000 dollars in a cryptocurrency scheme. Florida reported 350 AI-related complaints resulting in nearly 39.9 million dollars in losses, while Georgia reported 71 complaints totaling more than 10.4 million dollars in losses.

Scammers use generative AI to clone voices from social media, create fake photographs, spoof phone numbers, and impersonate trusted people in romance schemes and emergency situations like the grandparent scam. Experts note the technology makes traditional fraud harder to detect. To protect themselves, people should establish code words with family members, verify urgent requests by contacting individuals directly, avoid sending money based on phone calls alone, and report suspected scams to law enforcement and the FBI's Internet Crime Complaint Center.
